Updates for Winter Programming

Due to the recent increase in COVID-19 cases, Columbus Recreation and Parks Department is taking steps to ensure the health and safety of our participants and staff. Updates to our programs are outlined below:

Columbus Aquatics Center - Youth and adult swim lessons, stroke clinic and dive clinics are postponed one week to start the week of Jan. 10. Water aerobics, open swim and lap swim will go on as scheduled. Winter 2 classes registration opened yesterday and will start Jan. 31.

Community Centers - Winter Session classes will now start the week of Jan. 18. Registration will still open today, Jan. 4 at 12:30 p.m. To help limit direct contact with the public, we are asking participants to register online. In-person registrations can still be completed, but please stay home if you are sick or have any symptoms of COVID-19.

Cultural Arts Center - Session 1 classes will continue as planned. 

Fitness Resolution Solution - This event is being postponed. A new date will be announced soon.

Youth Basketball Leagues - League play will be postponed one week and will have new precautions; more detailed information will be sent directly to coaches, parents and guardians. Please check with your center for specific information and league schedules.

National Parks and Recreation Month

 

July is National Park and Recreation Month! Join Columbus Recreation and Parks Department as we celebrate our programs and services. From experiences in nature to favorite hobbies or physical activities, to special places to gather with family and friends, our parks, community centers and staff have played a central role in countless experiences and memories. In fact, throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, the increased time outdoors in nature helped many of our community members find a new appreciation for parks. 

This year’s theme is “Our Park and Recreation Story,” and we will be highlighting the Columbus Recreation and Parks programs, services and team members that help make our community stronger, more vibrant and more resilient. Water Safety Month

 

May is National Water Safety Month! As summer approaches, Columbus Recreation and Parks Department wants to highlight the importance of water safety and water competence.

Here are some tips to stay safe in the water this summer: 

  • Take swim lessons/learn to swim
  • Stay hydrated
  • Know your environment
  • Follow established rules
  • Be Alert; use active supervision
  • Wear your lifejacket in open water (lakes, oceans, etc.)
  • Use "touch" supervision

To learn more about water safety, check out these tips from American Red Cross.

Aquatics Study

Healthy Recipe

Spring Layered Smoothie

 

Ingredients: 

For the Romaine-Apple Layer

  • 1 heart of romaine lettuce, chopped
  • 1 Granny Smith apple, cored and chopped
  • 1 peeled and frozen banana, cut into chunks
  • 2 dates, pitted and chopped
  • 2 tablespoons parsley
  • 1/2 cup orange juice
  • Juice from 1 lime

For the Strawberry-Rhubarb Layer

  • 2 cups strawberries, sliced
  • 1 cup rhubarb, chopped
  • 1 peeled and frozen banana, cut into chunks
  • 2 dates, pitted and chopped
  • 5 ounces yogurt (I used non-fat vanilla yogurt)
  • 1/2 cup orange juice

Directions: 

  1. Make the romaine-apple layer. Add all of the ingredients for the romaine-apple layer to your blender. Blend on high until smooth. Divide the mixture evenly between two glasses. Rinse out the blender.
  2. Make the strawberry-rhubarb layer. Add all of the ingredients for the strawberry-rhubarb layer to your blender. Blend on high until smooth. Slowly pour the strawberry-rhubarb layer over the romaine-apple layer.
  3. Enjoy immediately.

Regular exercise can help put you back in control of your life.

If you’re not into regular exercise, putting together an exercise plan can be a bummer.

Remember though, that along with your diet and medications, regular physical activity is an important part of managing diabetes or dealing with prediabetes. When you’re active, your cells become more sensitive to insulin so it works more effectively. Plus, you just feel better and look better.

So, however you choose to exercise—taking regular walks around the block, going for a run, or signing up for a marathon—getting started is the most important part.

Get started. But get started safely.

It doesn’t matter where you are physically. If you’ve never set foot in a gym, that’s okay—as long as you start doing something now. If you haven’t been very active or are worried about your health, it’s important to consult your doctor and start slowly.

Light walking is a great place to start—and a great habit to incorporate into your life. Walk with a loved one or just by yourself while listening to an audio book. Set goals every day (distance walked, time spent walking, etc.) and do your best to meet them, and you’ll start feeling like you’re back in control of your life.

Even little changes make a big difference

If you’re still struggling with getting started or feeling overwhelmed by the idea of beginning a more active life,  take heart: every change, no matter how small, makes a difference in your ability to manage diabetes. Even losing 10-15 pounds can have a significant impact on your health. The power to change is firmly in your hands—so get moving today.

Building Resiliency in Children

This school year more than ever, it's become more important to build resiliency in children during these unpredictable times. Resiliency is the ability to adapt and manage difficult challenges. Resiliency can also be described as how you navigate through life while managing feelings of fear and anxiety in various situations. 

Here are some tips to help build resiliency in children: 

  • Change what you can and develop ways to cope with what you cannot

  • Pay attention to the thoughts you and your children have
